arxiv-2110-12114.title: Dense Dual-Attention Network for Light Field Image Super-Resolution
arxiv-2110-12114.creator: Yu Mo, Yingqian Wang, Chao Xiao, Jungang Yang, Wei An
arxiv-2110-12114.description: Abstract Light field (LF) images can be used to improve the performance of image super-resolution (SR) because both angular and spatial information is available. It is challenging to incorporate distinctive information from different views for LF image SR. Moreover, the long-term information from the previous layers can be weakened as the depth of network increases.

arxiv-2209-12960.description: Abstract . We consider the set of all the ideals of a ring, endowed with the coarse lower topology. arxiv-2412-12261.title: Gauge invariance and generalised η \eta regularisation
arxiv-2412-12261.creator: Antonio Padilla, and Robert G. C. Smith
arxiv-2412-12261.description: Abstract We generalise the η \eta regularisation scheme in order to develop a framework for systematically studying regularisation of loops in quantum field theory. This allows us to“solve” a set of gauge consistency conditions for families of gauge invariant regularisation schemes. We recover several known examples such as dimensional and denominator regularisations, as well as some more general solutions.

arxiv-2505-20276.title: Does quantization affect models’ performance on long-context tasks?
arxiv-2505-20276.creator: Anmol Mekala, Anirudh Atmakuru {amekala, aatmakuru}@umass.edu, [1ex] Yixiao Song, Marzena Karpinska, Mohit Iyyer yixiaosong@umass.edumkarpinska@microsoft.commiyyer@umd.edu
arxiv-2505-20276.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) now support context windows exceeding 128K tokens, but this comes with significant memory requirements and high inference latency. Quantization can mitigate these costs, but may degrade performance. In this work, we present the first systematic evaluation of quantized LLMs on tasks with long-inputs ( ≥ \geq 64K tokens) and long-form outputs. Our evaluation spans 9.

arxiv-2602-09404.creator: Somnath Dutta
arxiv-2602-09404.description: Abstract A fundamental challenge in star formation is understanding how a protostar accretes mass from its circumstellar disk while removing excess angular momentum. Protostellar jets are widely invoked as the primary channels for angular-momentum removal, yet the mechanism by which they are launched and extract angular momentum remains poorly constrained.

pmc-10587948.title: Assessing the utility of molecular diagnostic classification for cancers of unknown primary
pmc-10587948.creator: Elle C. Moore, Gerard C. Blobe, Nicholas C. DeVito, Brent A. Hanks, Michael R. Harrison, Christopher J. Hoimes, Jingquan Jia, Michael A. Morse, Parvathy Jayaprakasan, Andrew MacKelfresh, Hillary Mulder, Adam J. Hockenberry, Alia Zander, Martin C. Stumpe, Jackson Michuda, Kyle A. Beauchamp, Eric Pera
pmc-10587948.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). BackgroundRoughly 5% of metastatic cancers present with uncertain origin, for which molecular classification could influence subsequent management; however, prior studies of molecular diagnostic classifiers have reported mixed results with regard to clinical impact.

pmc-10708464.title: Field Manipulations in On-Chip Micro/Nanoscale Lasers Based on Colloid Nanocrystals
pmc-10708464.creator: Yazhou Gu, Zhengmei Yang, Zhitong Li
pmc-10708464.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Owning to merits such as bandgap tunability, solution processability, large absorption coefficients, and high photoluminescence quantum yields, colloidal quantum dots (CQDs) emerged as a promising gain material to make on-chip micro/nanoscale lasers with high silicon compatibility. In this paper, we review the recent progress in CQD on-chip micro/nanoscale lasers, with a special focus on the physical properties achieved through field manipulation schemes in different types of cavities.

pmc-11357393.title: Food Insecurity and Nutritional Inadequacy in Children and Adolescents of Basic Education Schools of Cantagalo District in São Tomé and Príncipe, Central Africa
pmc-11357393.creator: Francisca Ferreira, Maria Tavares, Renata Barros, Cláudia Camila Dias, Rita Morais, Madalena Ortigão, Patrícia Padrão, Mónica Rodrigues, Pedro Moreira
pmc-11357393.description: Food insecurity (FI) is a critical socioeconomic and public health problem globally, particularly affecting children’s nutritional status and development. This cross-sectional study aimed to assess the prevalence of nutritional inadequacy among children and adolescents in the Cantagalo district of São Tomé and Príncipe (STP), in Central Africa.

pmc-11640321.title: The Warmth of Sarudango: Modelling the Huddling Behaviour of Japanese Macaques (Macaca fuscata)
pmc-11640321.creator: Cédric Sueur, Shintaro Ishizuka, Yu Kaigaishi, Shinya Yamamoto
pmc-11640321.description: Simple SummaryJapanese macaques, also known as snow monkeys, are known for their ability to huddle together in cold weather to stay warm. However, the size of these huddling groups can vary greatly across different regions, with exceptionally large clusters observed on Shodoshima Island compared to smaller groups in colder areas.

pmc-11728795.title: Exploring Gluconamide-Modified Silica Nanoparticles of Different Sizes as Effective Carriers for Antimicrobial Photodynamic Therapy
pmc-11728795.creator: Ruth Prieto-Montero, Lucia Herrera, Maite Tejón, Andrea Albaya, Jose Luis Chiara, Mónica L Fanarraga, Virginia Martínez-Martínez, Aleš Panáček
pmc-11728795.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Antimicrobial resistance (AMR), a consequence of the ability of microorganisms, especially bacteria, to develop resistance against conventional antibiotics, hampering the treatment of common infections, is recognized as one of the most imperative health threats of this century. Antibacterial photodynamic therapy (aPDT) has emerged as a promising alternative strategy, utilizing photosensitizers activated by light to generate reactive oxygen species (ROS) that kill pathogens without inducing resistance.

pmc-12689866.title: Temporal dynamics and demographic specificity of provider-initiated HIV testing in China: an eight-year retrospective analysis
pmc-12689866.creator: Yuexin Sun, Qiaofang Wu, Yue Tao, Haoyue Yu, Ying Zhou, Jun Bao
pmc-12689866.description: BackgroundThis study evaluates the effectiveness of PITC implementation at Nanjing Drum Tower Hospital from 2017 to 2024 and examines variations in testing efficiency across different populations and time periods, aiming to provide critical evidence for adjusting PITC strategies to adapt to epidemiological changes.

pmc-12987515.title: Research progress on the compositional characteristics of the tumor immune microenvironment and immunopredictive models in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma
pmc-12987515.creator: Gongcheng Wang, Zhenzhen Li, Siyu Tan, Jing Ma, Zhiyong Yin, Juan Du, Linni Fan
pmc-12987515.description: Esophageal cancer is one of the most prevalent malignant tumors of the digestive tract, with esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) as its main histological type. In recent years, immunotherapeutic regimens centered on immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have achieved remarkable efficacy in patients with advanced ESCC.

pmc-13085274.title: Efficacy and safety of baclofen in the prophylaxis of postoperative nausea and vomiting after laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy: a randomized controlled trial
pmc-13085274.creator: Aya Gamal Moussa, Sahar Mohammed El-Haggar, Tamer Mosaad El-Mahdy, Tarek Mohamed Mostafa
pmc-13085274.description: BackgroundPostoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV) are among the most distressing aspects of the surgical experience, especially after laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy (LSG). This study evaluated the efficacy and safety of baclofen for preventing PONV in patients with morbid obesity undergoing LSG.

pmc-13180946.title: Bridging gaps between scientific research and regulatory decision-making in Europe: roles of academia, risk assessors, and policymakers
pmc-13180946.creator: Ana Fernandez-Agudo, Hannah Lester, Jose V. Tarazona, Fernando Rivero-Pino
pmc-13180946.description: A gap between scientific research and regulatory frameworks continues to challenge the effective translation of science into policy and regulation. This commentary explores the disconnection between scientific research, regulatory agencies, and policymakers, highlighting the distinct yet interdependent roles they play.

pmc-13558244.title: Integrative Multi-omics and Machine Learning Reveal the Therapeutic Mechanisms of Juanyu-Xiaozhi Formula in Metabolic Dysfunction-associated Steatotic Liver Disease and Hepatic Fibrosis via the AP-1/PPARγ/SCD1 Axis
pmc-13558244.creator: Zhiqiang Jin, Yi Huang, Cheng Zeng, Yueting Zhang, Yu Qiu, Yang Yang, Huabao Liu
pmc-13558244.description: Background and AimsDespite the surging global prevalence of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and related liver fibrosis, effective treatments remain limited. While the traditional Chinese medicine Juanyu-Xiaozhi Formula (JYXZF) is used against MASLD, its bioactive components and mechanisms are poorly understood. This study aimed to investigate the therapeutic effects of JYXZF and elucidate its underlying mechanisms of action.

uslaw-usc-t42-s8002.title: 42 U.S.C. § 8002 — Definitions
uslaw-usc-t42-s8002.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t42-s8002.description: United States Code, Title 42 (The Public Health And Welfare); Chapter 89 (Congregate Housing Services). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. For the purpose of this chapter— (1) the term “congregate housing” means (A) low-rent housing which, as of January 1, 1979, was built or under construction, with which there is connected a central dining facility where wholesome and economical meals can be.
